goal: Fixes a crash and a false 'corrupted database' failure when the assumeutxo snapshot base block was already stored on disk before the snapshot loaded.
Lets background validation resume normally instead of demanding a wasted -reindex.
reviewability: Ready to review, the flagged concern was answered by the author and nobody has revisited the rework since.
agreement: One reviewer questioned how often this edge case is hit (mzumsande); author explained the trigger path and rationale, no further pushback.
No other reviewer input; support has not been affirmed beyond that exchange.

result.summary: Fixes a bug where a node that has the assumeutxo snapshot base block on disk before loadtxoutset() runs can no longer make progress: background validation either hits a cursor assertion and aborts, or a restart triggers a false 'Corrupted block database' error demanding a reindex. The fix keeps the snapshot base block classified in the normal blockfile range rather than the ASSUMED range, adjusts FlushChainstateBlockFile, stops VerifyDB before disconnecting a snapshot base it cannot actually disconnect, and keeps the base in m_blocks_unlinked until its parents are processed. Functional test coverage is added for the base-already-on-disk scenario including a restart, and the wallet prune-height test is adjusted to match.
result.problem: Node operators (or software) that submit the snapshot base block locally via submitblock before calling loadtxoutset() end up in a state that either crashes the node (assertion failure) or bricks it on restart with a misleading 'reindex' message, even though the block database is not actually corrupt.

open_concerns: mzumsande questioned how common/motivated this scenario is, since normal P2P sync would already have the node close to the snapshot height; author clarified it is specifically about local submitblock/import before snapshot activation, not the common p2p path
resolved_concerns: Author explained the trigger clearly and reviewer did not push back further

categories.name: indexes
categories.evidence: Directly changes block/undo file storage classification (BlockfileTypeForHeight, FlushChainstateBlockFile, m_blockfile_cursors) in blockstorage.cpp/h, and carries the 'Block storage' label.
categories.rationale: Fixes an assertion crash in WriteBlockUndo and a false corruption message that sends operators to an unnecessary reindex, per the description: 'The block database is not corrupt, so the reindex that message asks for is wasted work.' The trigger condition is narrow (base block submitted locally before loadtxoutset), which keeps this from being P1.

categories.name: validation
categories.evidence: Changes chainstate block-index candidate logic (PopulateBlockIndexCandidates), VerifyDB's disconnect walk near the snapshot base, and FlushStateToDisk's flush-file selection, all core to assumeutxo background validation correctness.
categories.rationale: Prevents background validation from asserting/aborting and from VerifyDB attempting an impossible disconnect of the snapshot base, per the author: 'the base does have data, and no undo data... so the walk goes into it and the disconnect fails.' Reviewer mzumsande's question about how commonly this state arises supports treating it as a real but edge-case correctness fix rather than a mainline hazard, hence P2 not P1.

result.card: This PR fixes a real bug where a node that already has the assumeutxo snapshot base block on disk (e.g. via a local submitblock) before loadtxoutset() runs gets stuck: background validation either asserts and aborts (WriteBlockUndo cursor assertion) or, on restart, fails VerifyDB and tells the operator to reindex a database that is not actually corrupt. The fix reclassifies the snapshot base into the normal blockfile range, adjusts chainstate flush and VerifyDB logic accordingly, and keeps the base in m_blocks_unlinked until its parents are processed, with new functional test coverage for the scenario. The only reviewer (mzumsande) questioned how commonly this state is reached since normal p2p sync would already have the node near the snapshot height; the author clarified it applies specifically to local block submission before snapshot activation, and that explanation went unchallenged. The PR has been reworked and rebased several times, most recently 2026-08-19, with no further review since May. No PR dependency, but it touches areas that conflict with several other open PRs reworking blockstorage/validation error handling (#35731, #35714, #35646, #29700).
